MINUTES
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MAY 22, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City
Hall.

2.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Ciarolla, Griggs, Harik, Martin, Robinson,
  Shinn, Silvano, and Schachter
  Committee Members Absent:  Brtis, Medawar, and Nilsen
  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 27, 2023
  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH 27, 2023, EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
  NONE.

5.  STAFF ITEMS
A.  SHARING THE TRAILS SAFETY OUTREACH VIDEO SERIES
  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report and stated that
  Staff would be seeking volunteers from the Committee to appear in the videos.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER suggested using the crosswalk in front of City Hall at the
  intersection of Palos Verdes Drive North and Crenshaw Boulevard.
  MEMBER ROBINSON volunteered to assist and participate in the videos.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MAY 22, 2023
   MEMBER HARIK recommended adding that drivers not rev their engines when
  near a horse.
  MEMBER ROBINSON recommended splitting the first video into two videos, the
  first using the crosswalk and the second one featuring a message for drivers to
  slow down as the streets do not have sidewalks so they should be cautious and
  drive slowly.
  MEMBER CIAROLLA recommended shooting the second part of the first video
  on the Crenshaw Boulevard side.
  MEMBER SHINN inquired about the possibility of using a professional
  videographer. CHAIR SCHACHTER mentioned she could contact Jeff Koven to
  see if he would be able to assist and possibly donate his time.
  MEMBER SILVANO inquired about signage to deter drivers from honking their
  horns while driving.
  SUPERVISOR PINUELAS stated that Staff is looking for volunteers with horses
  from the Committee for the video in response to MEMBER SHINN.
  MEMBER HARIK volunteered to participate with her horse.
  Discussion ensued regarding potential ways to shoot the video regarding what do
  to when approaching behind a horse on a trail. CHAIR SCHACHTER
  recommended the video demonstrate the proper way to approach a horse.
  Supervisor Pinuelas recommended keeping the videos short since they would be
  posted on social media.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that videos two, three and four, could be done by
  focusing on filming the best behavior.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER and MEMBER ROBINSON volunteered to participate in the
  dog videos.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER suggested having a runner in running gear participate in the
  video regarding approaching a horse from behind. MEMBER SILVANO stated she
  could ask her husband to volunteer for that role as he runs the trails.
  MEMBER SHINN offered her horse for the videos.
  MEMBER SHINN recommended a video of a bicyclist riding on the trail toward a
  horse, share why bicycles are not allowed on the trails and then show the bicyclist
  existing the trail.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff recommended four videos based on time
  and resources but that additional videos could be done in response to MEMBER
  ROBINSON.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MAY 22, 2023
   CHAIR SCHACHTER clarified that all four videos were being considered and that
  videos two, three and four could be filmed in one day.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that a schedule has not been finalized but the plan is
  to film the videos this summer. In response to CHAIR SCHACHTER. Supervisor
  Pinuelas added that Staff could work around the availability of the videographer if
  needed.
B.  OVERVIEW OF BUSINESS LICENSING REQUIREMENTS
  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that outreach is done by business licensing to try to
  gain compliance in response to MEMBER SILVANO.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that business licensing fees range and are determined
  by the type of business, with some being based on gross receipts and other being
  flat fees in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER inquired about the potential of creating a category of
  business licensing for equine-related businesses similar to the horse trainer fees.
  MEMBER SILVANO stated that the taxes are determined by the voters, adding
  that the horse trainer permits are different because they include fees and taxes.
  Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed that the taxes are voted on and added that they are
  also determined by ordinance.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that a business license is required for doing business
  in the City regardless of the location of the business in response to MEMBER
  GRIGGS.
  Discussion ensued regarding monitoring and ensuring compliance of business
  licensing.
  MEMBER SILVANO stated that the City should actively seek compliance for all
  businesses, not just equestrian-related businesses.
  MEMBER CIAROLLA recommended the item be added to a future agenda.
  MEMBER SHINN concurred.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER directed Staff to provide examples of the categories and
  include examples of categories equestrian-related businesses might fall into.

C.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  MEMBER SHINN thanked Superintendent Goldsmith for the maintenance of the
  trails.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MAY 22, 2023
   MEMBER ROBINSON stated that there were two tree branches down on the trail
  at George F Canyon.

  MEMBER SILVANO inquired about Rachel Dwyer’s request for GGT footing at
  Dapplegray and asked if it had been addressed.

  Supervisor Pinuelas responded that she discussed the request with Ms. Dwyer
  and let her know that the footing was being changed (at Ernie Howlett Park Arena
  2) in partnership with the Portuguese Bend National Horse Show organizers and
  would not have been done without their commitment.

  MEMBER SILVANO recommended the City look into the potential of changing the
  footing at Dapplegray. Superintendent Goldsmith shared some challenges of doing
  so and factors to be considered such as the amount of water needed for GGT
  footing.

  Superintendent Goldsmith affirmed that the work being done at Dapplegray Arena
  includes replenishment of the sand in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  Supervisor Pinuelas and Superintendent Goldsmith affirmed that Ms. Dwyer is
  aware of the sand replenishment in response to MEMBER SHINN.

  MEMBER GRIGGS asked if the mustard on Fern Creek Trail is on the list for
  removal. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it is, but stated that Staff is
  waiting for new mower blades to come in before they can proceed with the work.

  MEMBER MARTIN inquired if Superintendent Goldsmith spoke to the Palos
  Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy about cutting back the trail behind the Empty
  Saddle Club. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that he did and that he dropped
  off four loads of soil so they could fill in the erosion.

D.  MAYOR’S RIDE DEBRIEF (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the event. She thanked MEMBER
  GRIGGS for helping the dignitaries get geared up for the ride and MEMBER
  SHINN for leading the community riders. She shared the dignitaries’ horses arrived
  late which prevented them from joining the group of community riders. Supervisor
  Pinuelas stated that Staff would work with the horse vendor to ensure they arrive
  on time next year. She stated that the event was successful overall and that the
  Scouts served approximately 700 breakfasts.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that next year, volunteers should be assigned to
  Arena 3 as the community riders tied their horses up on the rail, some close to

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MAY 22, 2023
   each other and near the sprinklers. He stated there were no issues but added
  having a couple volunteers would be good to ensure the safety of the horses.

  Discussion ensued regarding alternative trail horse vendors; however no
  recommendation was made.

E.  EQUESTRIAN RECOGNITION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas thanked Member Silvano for securing a donation for Carol
  Dean Porter’s plaque from the Peninsula Equestrian Circuit. She shared that a
  lower quote had been secured for the bronze plaque so the Peninsula Equestrian
  Circuit donated more than needed but those extra funds would go toward another
  project. Supervisor Pinuelas added that Staff would work on getting the bronze
  plaque ordered for Carol Dean Porter for the judges’ booth and the bench kit
  ordered for the Jan Ball project.

F.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update on this year’s plan for fireworks
  suppression. She stated that City staff is working with the Lomita Sheriff's station
  for fireworks suppression efforts with a dedicated task force of deputies assigned
  to respond to firework calls in the City during the holiday.
  She also stated that Staff would work with the Peter Weber Equestrian Center
  and Sanitation District in closing some gates early to prevent firework activity in
  the open space landfill areas.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if the trails at the top of the hill off Highridge Park
  belonged to the City. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that those are private
  property.

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that there are signs posted at the Masongate trail
  regarding the prohibition of motor vehicles but that many people still drive cars on
  the trail and drive fast.

  MEMBER SILVANO inquired about the possibility of adding an opening to the
  fence at the entrance to Rockbluff Park as an alternative to entering via the path.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MAY 22, 2023
   MEMBER ROBINSON commented that there are many e-bikes at the park and
  shared that she heard that there was an issue of items being removed from the
  maintenance yard.

  Superintendent Goldsmith shared that children were stealing items like lumber and
  constructing a tree house. He stated that the issue had been addressed adding
  that the Sheriff’s Posse had been notified and the structure removed.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if Code Enforcement could do anything to address
  the issue. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Sheriff Department had been
  responsive.

B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  MEMBER HARIK made a motion, seconded by MEMBER GRIGGS TO APPROVE
  AS FOLLOWS:
  CHAIR SCHACHTER ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:52 pm.
  There being no objections, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Pam Brown Schachter
  Community Services Supervisor  Chair

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MAY 22, 2023
